descriptionChirho: Adjective used in construct (יְלִיד / יְלִידֵי) meaning 'born of, native to,' describing persons born within a household or descended from a particular lineage. Occurs in singular construct (Gen 17:12-27, Lev 22:11) for a slave born in the master's house, and in plural construct (Gen 14:14, 17:23, Num 13:22, Josh 15:14, 2 Sam 21:16-18) for descendants or native-born inhabitants. English 'born of,' 'born ones of,' 'descendants of'; German Geborene(n); Arabic مولود/مواليد; Hindi जनम/जन्मे-हुए ('born/born ones'); Korean 태어난-자(들) ('born one(s)'). All four auto-clusters represent the same adjectival sense in different morphological forms (singular, plural, with prefixed prepositions ב among, ו and).
